papers.title: Natural Language Declarative Prompting (NLD-P): A Modular Governance Method for Prompt Design Under Model Drift
papers.abstract: The rapid evolution of large language models (LLMs) has transformed prompt engineering from a localized craft into a systems-level governance challenge. As models scale and update across generations, prompt behavior becomes sensitive to shifts in instruction-following policies, alignment regimes, and decoding strategies, a phenomenon we characterize as GPT-scale model drift. Under such conditions, surface-level formatting conventions and ad hoc refinement are insufficient to ensure stable, interpretable control. This paper reconceptualizes Natural Language Declarative Prompting (NLD-P) as a declarative governance method rather than a rigid field template. NLD-P is formalized as a modular control abstraction that separates provenance, constraint logic, task content, and post-generation evaluation, encoded directly in natural language without reliance on external orchestration code. We define minimal compliance criteria, analyze model-dependent schema receptivity, and position NLD-P as an accessible governance framework for non-developer practitioners operating within evolving LLM ecosystems. Portions of drafting and editorial refinement employed a schema-bound LLM assistant configured under NLD-P. All conceptual framing, methodological claims, and final revisions were directed, reviewed, and approved by the human author under a documented human-in-the-loop protocol. The paper concludes by outlining implications for declarative control under ongoing model evolution and identifying directions for future empirical validation.
papers.headline: AIの更新に振り回されず、指示書を安定運用できる
papers.one_liner: AIの性能や種類が変わっても動作を安定させるため、指示（プロンプト）を役割ごとに部品化して管理する手法です。コードを書かずに言葉だけで、AIの「思い込み（ハルシネーション）」を防ぎ、誰でも高度な制御が可能になります。
key_points: AIがアップデートされても業務フローが壊れにくくなり、再設定の手間を減らせる
指示を「背景」「ルール」「タスク」「評価」に分解するため、一部の修正だけで全体を調整できる
プログラミングの知識がなくても、日本語の指示書だけでAIの挙動を厳密に管理（ガバナンス）できる
AIが出した回答がルール通りか、AI自身にセルフチェックさせる仕組みを簡単に組み込める
複数のAIを使い分ける際も、指示書の部品を使い回せるため、コストや精度の比較が容易になる
who_should_read: PM/プロダクトマネージャー
application_ideas: 建築基準法の改正時に、図面チェックAIの「法規ルール部品」だけを更新し、判定ロジックを即座に最新化する。
インフラ点検でAIのバージョンが変わっても、「異常の判定基準」を記述した部品を使い回すことで、過去の点検データとの一貫性を保つ。
現場ごとに異なる作業手順書をAIに読み込ませる際、共通の「安全管理ルール」を部品として組み込み、全社で一貫した安全基準を維持する。

papers.title: DySL-VLA: Efficient Vision-Language-Action Model Inference via Dynamic-Static Layer-Skipping for Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown remarkable success in robotic tasks like manipulation by fusing a language model's reasoning with a vision model's 3D understanding. However, their high computational cost remains a major obstacle for real-world applications that require real-time performance. We observe that the actions within a task have varying levels of importance: critical steps demand high precision, while less important ones can tolerate more variance. Leveraging this insight, we propose DySL-VLA, a novel framework that addresses computational cost by dynamically skipping VLA layers based on each action's importance. DySL-VLA categorizes its layers into two types: informative layers, which are consistently executed, and incremental layers, which can be selectively skipped. To intelligently skip layers without sacrificing accuracy, we invent a prior-post skipping guidance mechanism to determine when to initiate layer-skipping. We also propose a skip-aware two-stage knowledge distillation algorithm to efficiently train a standard VLA into a DySL-VLA. Our experiments indicate that DySL-VLA achieves 2.1% improvement in success length over Deer-VLA on the Calvin dataset, while simultaneously reducing trainable parameters by a factor of 85.7 and providing a 3.75x speedup relative to the RoboFlamingo baseline at iso-accuracy. Our code is available on https://github.com/PKU-SEC-Lab/DYSL_VLA.
papers.headline: 重要度に合わせて計算を賢くサボり、ロボットを3.7倍速く動かす
papers.one_liner: ロボットが周囲を見て言葉で動くAI（VLAモデル）において、精密さが不要な動作では計算を「手抜き（レイヤースキップ）」する仕組みにより、精度を保ったまま動作を3.75倍高速化する技術です。
key_points: 「慎重に動くべき場面」と「適当で良い場面」をAIが自動で判別し、計算量を柔軟に調整できる
従来モデルと比較して、動作の成功率を維持・向上（+2.1%）させつつ処理速度を劇的に高めた
学習が必要なAIの内部部品（パラメータ）を約85分の1にまで削減し、軽量化に成功した
高性能な大型AIの知識を、効率よく高速版AIへと移植（知識蒸留）する新しい訓練手法を開発
リアルタイム性が求められる現場で、高価な計算機なしでも高度なロボット操作が可能になる
who_should_read: PM/プロダクトマネージャー
application_ideas: 工場のピッキングロボットにおいて、部品に近づくまでは「高速モード」、掴む瞬間だけ「精密モード」に切り替えることで、作業サイクルを短縮する
インフラ点検ドローンが、移動中はバッテリー節約のために簡易計算で行い、異常検知時のみフルパワーで画像解析を行うことで稼働時間を延ばす
建設現場の資材運搬ロボットにおいて、障害物のない直線路では計算を省略し、人混みや複雑な路面ではフル計算で安全を確保する動的な制御に活用する

papers.title: SC-Arena: A Natural Language Benchmark for Single-Cell Reasoning with Knowledge-Augmented Evaluation
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied in scientific research, offering new capabilities for knowledge discovery and reasoning. In single-cell biology, however, evaluation practices for both general and specialized LLMs remain inadequate: existing benchmarks are fragmented across tasks, adopt formats such as multiple-choice classification that diverge from real-world usage, and rely on metrics lacking interpretability and biological grounding. We present SC-ARENA, a natural language evaluation framework tailored to single-cell foundation models. SC-ARENA formalizes a virtual cell abstraction that unifies evaluation targets by representing both intrinsic attributes and gene-level interactions. Within this paradigm, we define five natural language tasks (cell type annotation, captioning, generation, perturbation prediction, and scientific QA) that probe core reasoning capabilities in cellular biology. To overcome the limitations of brittle string-matching metrics, we introduce knowledge-augmented evaluation, which incorporates external ontologies, marker databases, and scientific literature to support biologically faithful and interpretable judgments. Experiments and analysis across both general-purpose and domain-specialized LLMs demonstrate that (i) under the Virtual Cell unified evaluation paradigm, current models achieve uneven performance on biologically complex tasks, particularly those demanding mechanistic or causal understanding; and (ii) our knowledge-augmented evaluation framework ensures biological correctness, provides interpretable, evidence-grounded rationales, and achieves high discriminative capacity, overcoming the brittleness and opacity of conventional metrics. SC-Arena thus provides a unified and interpretable framework for assessing LLMs in single-cell biology, pointing toward the development of biology-aligned, generalizable foundation models.
papers.headline: AIが専門知識を正しく理解しているか自動で判定できる
papers.one_liner: 生命科学の分野で、AIが単にそれらしい回答（AIの思い込み）をしているだけなのか、専門知識データベース（外部知識）に基づき細胞の仕組みを正しく推論できているかを厳密に評価する仕組みです。
key_points: AIが「知ったかぶり」をせず、科学的な根拠に基づいて回答しているかを数値化できます。
「もし特定の遺伝子に変化が起きたらどうなるか」といった、将来の予測や変化（シミュレーション）の正確性を測れます。
単なる単語の一致ではなく、専門書や論文などの外部データと照らし合わせて意味の正しさを採点できます。
AIの回答に対して「なぜ正しいのか」「どこが根拠に反するか」という解説付きの評価が得られます。
画像的なデータ（細胞の状態）と言葉による説明（専門用語）を、AIがどれほど結びつけられているかを多角的に確認できます。
tags: バイオ・ライフサイエンスAI
性能評価フレームワーク
who_should_read: PM/プロダクトマネージャー
application_ideas: 【インフラ点検】「もしこのひび割れを放置したら、5年後にどうなるか」という劣化予測に対し、AIの回答が過去の点検指針や物理学的な根拠に基づいているかを自動評価する仕組み。
【図面チェック】建築基準法や社内ルールを「外部知識」として登録し、AIが図面の不備を指摘した際に、どの法規のどの条文に基づいた判断かをセットで提示・評価する機能。
【工場検査】製造装置の異音や振動データから故障原因を推論するAIにおいて、単なる確率的な判定ではなく、マニュアルや修理履歴に照らして「機構上の因果関係」を正しく説明できているかの検証。

papers.title: Test-Time Scaling with Diffusion Language Models via Reward-Guided Stitching
papers.abstract: Reasoning with large language models often benefits from generating multiple chains-of-thought, but existing aggregation strategies are typically trajectory-level (e.g., selecting the best trace or voting on the final answer), discarding useful intermediate work from partial or "nearly correct" attempts. We propose Stitching Noisy Diffusion Thoughts, a self-consistency framework that turns cheap diffusion-sampled reasoning into a reusable pool of step-level candidates. Given a problem, we (i) sample many diverse, low-cost reasoning trajectories using a masked diffusion language model, (ii) score every intermediate step with an off-the-shelf process reward model (PRM), and (iii) stitch these highest-quality steps across trajectories into a composite rationale. This rationale then conditions an autoregressive (AR) model (solver) to recompute only the final answer. This modular pipeline separates exploration (diffusion) from evaluation and solution synthesis, avoiding monolithic unified hybrids while preserving broad search. Across math reasoning benchmarks, we find that step-level recombination is most beneficial on harder problems, and ablations highlight the importance of the final AR solver in converting stitched but imperfect rationales into accurate answers. Using low-confidence diffusion sampling with parallel, independent rollouts, our training-free framework improves average accuracy by up to 23.8% across six math and coding tasks. At the same time, it achieves up to a 1.8x latency reduction relative to both traditional diffusion models (e.g., Dream, LLaDA) and unified architectures (e.g., TiDAR). Code is available at https://github.com/roymiles/diffusion-stitching.
papers.headline: 「惜しい回答」を切り貼りしAIの正解率と速度を大幅に上げる
papers.one_liner: 失敗した複数の推論プロセスから「正しい部分」だけを自動で抽出し、パズルのように組み合わせて（ステッチング）完璧な回答を作る技術です。これにより、数学やコーディングなどの難問に対して、既存手法より最大23.8%高い精度と1.8倍のスピードを両立できます。
key_points: 「ほぼ正解」なのにボツにされていた中間プロセスを捨てずに有効活用できる
AIモデルを一から作り直す（追加学習）必要がなく、既存のモデルを組み合わせるだけで導入できる
画像生成で使われる「拡散モデル」の言語版を用いることで、大量の回答案を高速かつ安価に作成できる
複数の回答案から「良いとこ取り」をするため、AIの思い込み（ハルシネーション）による間違いを抑制できる
論理的な計算や複雑な手順が必要なタスクほど、従来の手法よりも劇的な改善が見込める
who_should_read: PM/プロダクトマネージャー
application_ideas: 橋梁や道路の点検レポート作成において、AIが生成した複数の不完全な根拠から「正しい手順」だけを繋ぎ合わせ、専門家レベルの精緻な報告書を自動構成する。
複雑な意匠図と構造図の整合性チェックで、AIが提示した複数の矛盾指摘の中から確実性の高いステップを統合し、手戻りのない修正指示書を生成する。
工場の設備故障時の復旧ガイド作成において、過去の膨大な事例から有効な対処ステップを「良いとこ取り」して、現場作業員が迷わない最短の復旧手順を提示する。

papers.title: A Holistic Framework for Robust Bangla ASR and Speaker Diarization with Optimized VAD and CTC Alignment
papers.abstract: Despite being one of the most widely spoken languages globally, Bangla remains a low-resource language in the field of Natural Language Processing (NLP). Mainstream Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and Speaker Diarization systems for Bangla struggles when processing longform audio exceeding 3060 seconds. This paper presents a robust framework specifically engineered for extended Bangla content by leveraging preexisting models enhanced with novel optimization pipelines for the DL Sprint 4.0 contest. Our approach utilizes Voice Activity Detection (VAD) optimization and Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) segmentation via forced word alignment to maintain temporal accuracy and transcription integrity over long durations. Additionally, we employed several finetuning techniques and preprocessed the data using augmentation techniques and noise removal. By bridging the performance gap in complex, multi-speaker environments, this work provides a scalable solution for real-world, longform Bangla speech applications.
papers.headline: ベンガル語の長い会議も誰が話したか正確に記録できるようになる
papers.one_liner: ベンガル語の長い会話（60秒以上）において、誰が話しているかを識別（話者分離）しながら正確にテキスト化（自動音声認識）する技術です。無音部分を正しく見極める機能や、音と文字をピッタリ合わせる技術（強制アライメント）を組み合わせることで、雑音の多い環境でも精度の高い記録を実現します。
key_points: 60秒を超える長い音声でも、途中でエラーにならず最後まで文字に起こせる
複数人が同時に話す環境でも、誰の発言かを正確に区別して記録できる
周囲の騒音を自動で取り除き、必要な声だけをクリアに拾い上げられる
文字と音声のタイミングがズレないため、後から録音を確認する手間が省ける
これまでAI開発が難しかった言語でも、実用レベルの精度で運用できる
who_should_read: PM/プロダクトマネージャー
application_ideas: 外国人労働者が多い建設現場で、ベンガル語などの指示内容を自動で記録し、即座に日本語へ翻訳して共有する仕組みに活用できる
騒音が激しい工場内での点検作業中に、作業者が発した音声メモをノイズ除去技術で正確にテキスト化し、報告書作成を自動化する
インフラ点検の現場で、複数人の調査員が会話しながら行う状況確認を、誰がどの異常を指摘したか紐付けて自動記録する

papers.title: Align then Adapt: Rethinking Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning in 4D Perception
papers.abstract: Point cloud video understanding is critical for robotics as it accurately encodes motion and scene interaction. We recognize that 4D datasets are far scarcer than 3D ones, which hampers the scalability of self-supervised 4D models. A promising alternative is to transfer 3D pre-trained models to 4D perception tasks. However, rigorous empirical analysis reveals two critical limitations that impede transfer capability: overfitting and the modality gap. To overcome these challenges, we develop a novel "Align then Adapt" (PointATA) paradigm that decomposes parameter-efficient transfer learning into two sequential stages. Optimal-transport theory is employed to quantify the distributional discrepancy between 3D and 4D datasets, enabling our proposed point align embedder to be trained in Stage 1 to alleviate the underlying modality gap. To mitigate overfitting, an efficient point-video adapter and a spatial-context encoder are integrated into the frozen 3D backbone to enhance temporal modeling capacity in Stage 2. Notably, with the above engineering-oriented designs, PointATA enables a pre-trained 3D model without temporal knowledge to reason about dynamic video content at a smaller parameter cost compared to previous work. Extensive experiments show that PointATA can match or even outperform strong full fine-tuning models, whilst enjoying the advantage of parameter efficiency, e.g. 97.21 \% accuracy on 3D action recognition, $+8.7 \%$ on 4 D action segmentation, and 84.06\% on 4D semantic segmentation.
papers.headline: 静止画AIが低コストで「動き」を理解し、現場の異変を見抜く
papers.one_liner: 3Dの静止データ（3D点群）で学んだAIに対し、最小限の追加学習（パラメーター効率的な転移学習）を行うだけで、時間の経過を伴う「動き（4D）」まで高精度に判別できるようになります。
key_points: 膨大で準備が難しい「動画データ」が少なくても、既存の静止画AI資産を有効活用できる
AIの「思い込み（過学習）」を防ぎながら、動的なシーンの理解力を大幅に引き上げられる
静止画と動画の間の「データの見え方の違い」をAIが自動で補正して橋渡しする
一からAIを作り直す必要がないため、計算コストを抑えつつ短期間で導入準備ができる
作業の工程変化や、物体の変形など、時間の流れを含めた複雑な変化を正確に捉えられる
who_should_read: PM/プロダクトマネージャー
application_ideas: 建設現場の4D進捗管理において、定期的な3Dスキャンデータを「動画」として解析し、設計図面とのズレや施工の遅れを自動で早期発見する。
工場の自動検査ラインで、製品の組み立て工程（動き）を3Dで追跡し、ネジ締め不足や部品の取り付け順序の間違いをリアルタイムで判定する。
インフラ点検において、橋梁や法面の経時的な形状変化を4D解析し、肉眼では気づきにくい微細な歪みの進行や崩落の予兆を検知する。

papers.title: Retrieve and Segment: Are a Few Examples Enough to Bridge the Supervision Gap in Open-Vocabulary Segmentation?
papers.abstract: Open-vocabulary segmentation (OVS) extends the zero-shot recognition capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs) to pixel-level prediction, enabling segmentation of arbitrary categories specified by text prompts. Despite recent progress, OVS lags behind fully supervised approaches due to two challenges: the coarse image-level supervision used to train VLMs and the semantic ambiguity of natural language. We address these limitations by introducing a few-shot setting that augments textual prompts with a support set of pixel-annotated images. Building on this, we propose a retrieval-augmented test-time adapter that learns a lightweight, per-image classifier by fusing textual and visual support features. Unlike prior methods relying on late, hand-crafted fusion, our approach performs learned, per-query fusion, achieving stronger synergy between modalities. The method supports continually expanding support sets, and applies to fine-grained tasks such as personalized segmentation. Experiments show that we significantly narrow the gap between zero-shot and supervised segmentation while preserving open-vocabulary ability.
papers.headline: 数枚のお手本でAIの勘違いを防ぎ、自由な対象を正確に切り出す
papers.one_liner: 言葉の指示に加え、数枚の「お手本画像（ピクセル単位の正解付き）」を組み合わせることで、AIが初めて見る物体でも正確にその形を抽出（セグメンテーション）できるようになる技術です。AIが言葉と画像の両方の情報をその場で融合して判断を調整する仕組み（テストタイムアダプター）により、精度の高い切り出しを実現します。
key_points: 言葉（テキスト）だけでは伝わりにくい曖昧な対象でも、数枚の画像を見せることで「これと同じもの」と正確に認識できる。
数万枚の学習データは不要で、現場で用意した数枚の注釈付き画像（お手本）があれば、すぐに特殊な部品や損傷の特定を開始できる。
特定の現場や製品に特化した「パーソナライズ（個別最適化）」された認識が、大規模な再学習なしに可能になる。
運用しながらお手本画像を後から追加・更新できるため、使えば使うほど現場の状況に即した高精度なAIに進化する。
従来のAIの「思い込み（ハルシネーション）」による誤判定を、実際の手本を見せることで強力に抑制し、信頼性を高められる。
who_should_read: PM/プロダクトマネージャー
application_ideas: 工場の品質検査の場面で、新製品の「微細な傷」を検出する際、数枚の良品・不良品写真をお手本として読み込ませることで、大規模な再学習なしに即座に高精度な自動検査ラインを構築できる。
橋梁やトンネルの点検において、現場特有の汚れと「本当のひび割れ」の判別が難しい際、過去の類似事例数枚をAIに参照させて判定させることで、見落としを激減させ点検作業を効率化できる。
BIM/CIM活用の場面で、現場写真の中にある「特殊な設備機器」を、メーカー提供の数枚のカタログ画像をもとにAIに自動抽出させ、3Dモデル上の配置位置と自動で突合する仕組みに使える。

papers.title: A Mixture-of-Experts Model for Multimodal Emotion Recognition in Conversations
papers.abstract: Emotion Recognition in Conversations (ERC) presents unique challenges, requiring models to capture the temporal flow of multi-turn dialogues and to effectively integrate cues from multiple modalities. We propose Mixture of Speech-Text Experts for Recognition of Emotions (MiSTER-E), a modular Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) framework designed to decouple two core challenges in ERC: modality-specific context modeling and multimodal information fusion. MiSTER-E leverages large language models (LLMs) fine-tuned for both speech and text to provide rich utterance-level embeddings, which are then enhanced through a convolutional-recurrent context modeling layer. The system integrates predictions from three experts-speech-only, text-only, and cross-modal-using a learned gating mechanism that dynamically weighs their outputs. To further encourage consistency and alignment across modalities, we introduce a supervised contrastive loss between paired speech-text representations and a KL-divergence-based regulariza-tion across expert predictions. Importantly, MiSTER-E does not rely on speaker identity at any stage. Experiments on three benchmark datasets-IEMOCAP, MELD, and MOSI-show that our proposal achieves 70.9%, 69.5%, and 87.9% weighted F1-scores respectively, outperforming several baseline speech-text ERC systems. We also provide various ablations to highlight the contributions made in the proposed approach.
papers.headline: 声と言葉を組み合わせて、会話相手の感情を正確に理解できる
papers.one_liner: 音声とテキストのそれぞれに特化した「AIの専門家チーム（Mixture-of-Experts）」が、会話の流れやトーンを分析して感情を特定します。話し手が誰かを事前に教えなくても（匿名でも）、声の調子と言葉の意味の両方から高精度な判断が可能です。
key_points: 「声のトーン」と「話の内容」を別々の専門AIが分析し、最後に統合して判断するため見落としが少ない
単発の発言だけでなく、会話の前後の流れ（文脈）を汲み取って感情を判定できる
話し手を特定する情報が不要なので、プライバシーに配慮が必要な現場でも導入しやすい
「文字では怒っているが、声は冷静」といった矛盾する状況でも、AIが重要度を自動調整して正解を導く
最新の言語モデル（LLM）をベースにしているため、日常的な話し言葉の微妙なニュアンスも理解できる
tags: コミュニケーション解析
who_should_read: PM/プロダクトマネージャー
application_ideas: 建設現場の遠隔安全パトロールで、現場監督と作業員の会話から「焦り」や「疲労」を検知し、事故を未然に防ぐアラートを出す
工場の設備保全の引き継ぎ会議を分析し、マニュアル化しづらい「懸念点」や「違和感」を技術者が口にした瞬間を特定して共有する
インフラ点検報告の音声ログから、点検員の「自信のなさ」や「迷い」を検出し、特に再確認が必要な箇所を優先順位付けする

papers.title: OmniGAIA: Towards Native Omni-Modal AI Agents
papers.abstract: Human intelligence naturally intertwines omni-modal perception -- spanning vision, audio, and language -- with complex reasoning and tool usage to interact with the world. However, current multi-modal LLMs are primarily confined to bi-modal interactions (e.g., vision-language), lacking the unified cognitive capabilities required for general AI assistants. To bridge this gap, we introduce OmniGAIA, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate omni-modal agents on tasks necessitating deep reasoning and multi-turn tool execution across video, audio, and image modalities. Constructed via a novel omni-modal event graph approach, OmniGAIA synthesizes complex, multi-hop queries derived from real-world data that require cross-modal reasoning and external tool integration. Furthermore, we propose OmniAtlas, a native omni-modal foundation agent under tool-integrated reasoning paradigm with active omni-modal perception. Trained on trajectories synthesized via a hindsight-guided tree exploration strategy and OmniDPO for fine-grained error correction, OmniAtlas effectively enhances the tool-use capabilities of existing open-source models. This work marks a step towards next-generation native omni-modal AI assistants for real-world scenarios.
papers.headline: 「目・耳・知識」を使い分け、現場の複雑な依頼に応えるAI
papers.one_liner: 映像・音声・画像を同時に理解し、さらに自ら道具（外部ツール）を使いこなして問題を解決する、より人間に近いAIアシスタント（オムニモーダル・エージェント）の技術です。
key_points: 動画・音声・画像をひとまとめに処理し、状況を多角的に把握できる
AIが自分で適切なツール（検索や計算など）を選び、複雑な課題を自律的に解決できる
「動画内の異音と視覚的な異常を照らし合わせる」といった高度な判断が可能になる
失敗から学習して間違いを自分自身で修正する仕組みにより、回答の正確性が高い
現実世界の複雑なトラブルを再現したテストで、従来モデルを超える実力を証明した
who_should_read: PM/プロダクトマネージャー
application_ideas: インフラ点検：ドローン映像の「ひび割れ」とマイクが拾った「打音の異音」を統合解析し、内部の空洞化リスクを自動判定する。
工場安全管理：防犯カメラの映像で転倒を検知しつつ、同時に「助けて」という声をマイクで拾い、即座に最適な救助ルートを案内する。
技能伝承：ベテランの作業動画と説明音声をAIが学習し、新人の作業をリアルタイムで見守りながら「今の音は締め付けが甘い」と音声で指導する。

papers.title: AMA-Bench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Memory for Agentic Applications
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are deployed as autonomous agents in increasingly complex applications, where enabling long-horizon memory is critical for achieving strong performance. However, a significant gap exists between practical applications and current evaluation standards for agent memory: existing benchmarks primarily focus on dialogue-centric, human-agent interactions. In reality, agent memory consists of a continuous stream of agent-environment interactions that are primarily composed of machine-generated representations. To bridge this gap, we introduce AMA-Bench (Agent Memory with Any length), which evaluates long-horizon memory for LLMs in real agentic applications. It features two key components: (1) a set of real-world agentic trajectories across representative agentic applications, paired with expert-curated QA, and (2) a set of synthetic agentic trajectories that scale to arbitrary horizons, paired with rule-based QA. Our comprehensive study shows that existing memory systems underperform on AMA-Bench primarily because they lack causality and objective information and are constrained by the lossy nature of similarity-based retrieval employed by many memory systems. To address these limitations, we propose AMA-Agent, an effective memory system featuring a causality graph and tool-augmented retrieval. Our results demonstrate that AMA-Agent achieves 57.22% average accuracy on AMA-Bench, surpassing the strongest memory system baselines by 11.16%.
papers.headline: 複雑な連続作業でも、AIが過去の手順や目的を忘れなくなる
papers.one_liner: AIが長時間にわたる複雑な作業（エージェント行動）の履歴を、「原因と結果のつながり（因果関係）」として整理して記憶し、必要な時に正確に思い出せる技術です。
key_points: 数千ステップに及ぶ長い作業工程でも、過去の重要な判断や操作を忘れずに参照できます。
単なる言葉の「似ている度合い」での検索ではなく、作業の前後関係を理解して情報を探せます。
「なぜその操作をしたか」という因果関係をグラフ構造で記録するため、AIの思い込みによるミスが減ります。
現実の複雑な業務シナリオに基づいた評価指標により、現場投入時の実用性を精度高く測定できます。
外部ツールを組み合わせて過去の記録を掘り起こす仕組みにより、膨大なログから必要な情報をピンポイントで見つけられます。
who_should_read: PM/プロダクトマネージャー
application_ideas: インフラ点検の場面で、過去10年分の点検・補修履歴の「つながり」をAIが把握し、今回のひび割れが過去のどの補修ミスに起因するかを即座に特定する。
大規模なBIMモデルの編集において、数ヶ月にわたる設計変更の経緯（誰が、なぜ、どの部品を変更したか）を作業ログから自動で整理し、設計矛盾の根本原因を突き止める。
工場の製造ラインで、熟練工の長時間の操作ログをAIが解析し、「エラー発生の数時間前に起きていた微小な変化」と「その後のトラブル」の因果関係を特定して後継者に指導する。

papers.title: SettleFL: Trustless and Scalable Reward Settlement Protocol for Federated Learning on Permissionless Blockchains (Extended version)
papers.abstract: In open Federated Learning (FL) environments where no central authority exists, ensuring collaboration fairness relies on decentralized reward settlement, yet the prohibitive cost of permissionless blockchains directly clashes with the high-frequency, iterative nature of model training. Existing solutions either compromise decentralization or suffer from scalability bottlenecks due to linear on-chain costs. To address this, we present SettleFL, a trustless and scalable reward settlement protocol designed to minimize total economic friction by offering a family of two interoperable protocols. Leveraging a shared domain-specific circuit architecture, SettleFL offers two interoperable strategies: (1) a Commit-and-Challenge variant that minimizes on-chain costs via optimistic execution and dispute-driven arbitration, and (2) a Commit-with-Proof variant that guarantees instant finality through per-round validity proofs. This design allows the protocol to flexibly adapt to varying latency and cost constraints while enforcing rational robustness without trusted coordination. We conduct extensive experiments combining real FL workloads and controlled simulations. Results show that SettleFL remains practical when scaling to 800 participants, achieving substantially lower gas cost.
papers.headline: 社外秘データを守りつつ、AI学習の貢献度へ自動で報酬を支払える
papers.one_liner: データを手元に残したまま複数人でAIを育てる「連合学習（データを外に出さずにみんなでAIを賢くする手法）」において、中央管理者がいなくても、貢献度に応じた報酬を「改ざんできないブロックチェーン」を通じて安価かつ正確に分配できる仕組みです。
key_points: 報酬を管理する「元締め」が不要なため、特定の企業に利益を搾取される心配がありません。
ブロックチェーンの利用手数料（ガス代）を大幅に削減でき、800人規模の大人数でも現実的なコストで運用できます。
「異常があった時だけ確認する」方式と「都度証明書を出す」方式を使い分け、スピードと正確性を両立できます。
手抜きや偽のデータで報酬をだまし取ろうとする「不正な参加者」を自動的に排除する仕組みを備えています。
競合他社同士でも、お互いのデータを守りながら共同で高性能なAIを開発するビジネスモデルが構築可能です。
who_should_read: PM/プロダクトマネージャー
application_ideas: インフラ点検コンソーシアムの場面で、競合する点検会社同士が橋梁の損傷画像を持ち寄り、共通の劣化検知AIを作成。提供した画像の質と量に応じて、ブロックチェーン経由で利用料の配当を自動分配することで、データ提供のモチベーションを高める。
工場の外観検査AI開発において、複数の中小企業が自社のNG画像データを外に出さずに共有学習に参加。AI精度向上への貢献度を「証明書」として発行し、次回の保守契約の割引やトークン報酬として還元する。
BIM/CIMデータの活用シーンで、各設計事務所が持つ秘匿性の高い3Dモデルのノウハウを、データを秘匿したまま学習。成果物のAIモデルが使われるたびに、学習に寄与した各社へスマートコントラクト（自動契約）で対価を支払う仕組みを作る。

papers.title: ManifoldGD: Training-Free Hierarchical Manifold Guidance for Diffusion-Based Dataset Distillation
papers.abstract: In recent times, large datasets hinder efficient model training while also containing redundant concepts. Dataset distillation aims to synthesize compact datasets that preserve the knowledge of large-scale training sets while drastically reducing storage and computation. Recent advances in diffusion models have enabled training-free distillation by leveraging pre-trained generative priors; however, existing guidance strategies remain limited. Current score-based methods either perform unguided denoising or rely on simple mode-based guidance toward instance prototype centroids (IPC centroids), which often are rudimentary and suboptimal. We propose Manifold-Guided Distillation (ManifoldGD), a training-free diffusion-based framework that integrates manifold consistent guidance at every denoising timestep. Our method employs IPCs computed via a hierarchical, divisive clustering of VAE latent features, yielding a multi-scale coreset of IPCs that captures both coarse semantic modes and fine intra-class variability. Using a local neighborhood of the extracted IPC centroids, we create the latent manifold for each diffusion denoising timestep. At each denoising step, we project the mode-alignment vector onto the local tangent space of the estimated latent manifold, thus constraining the generation trajectory to remain manifold-faithful while preserving semantic consistency. This formulation improves representativeness, diversity, and image fidelity without requiring any model retraining. Empirical results demonstrate consistent gains over existing training-free and training-based baselines in terms of FID, l2 distance among real and synthetic dataset embeddings, and classification accuracy, establishing ManifoldGD as the first geometry-aware training-free data distillation framework.
papers.headline: 膨大な学習データを「いいとこ取り」してAI開発を高速化
papers.one_liner: 大量の画像データから「エッセンス」だけを抽出した少数のデータセットを、AIの追加学習（ファインチューニング）なしで自動作成できる技術です。画像生成AIが持つ「データの法則性（マニフォールド）」を賢く利用することで、高品質で多様な練習問題をAIに効率的に与えられます。
key_points: 数万枚のデータを数百枚に「濃縮」しても、AIの判定精度を高く維持できる
追加の学習（ファインチューニング）が一切不要なため、導入コストを抑えられる
データの「典型例」だけでなく「細かなバリエーション」も漏らさず抽出できる
AIが学習しやすい「高品質でノイズの少ない画像」を生成し、学習効率を高める
ストレージ容量や計算リソースを節約でき、モバイル端末などへのAI実装を助ける
who_should_read: PM/プロダクトマネージャー
application_ideas: インフラ点検の場面で、過去数十年分の膨大なひび割れ写真から「典型的な劣化パターン」を100枚に凝縮し、現場のタブレットでも高速に動作する判定AIを構築する。
工場の品質検査において、数万点の正常品の画像から「合格基準のバリエーション」を代表的な数枚に要約し、新しい製造ラインへのAI導入期間を大幅に短縮する。
BIM/CIMの活用において、膨大な3Dモデルから生成した2D画像を整理し、現場の機材を識別するための「最小かつ最強の学習用図鑑」を自動作成する。

papers.title: Sequential Regression for Continuous Value Prediction using Residual Quantization
papers.abstract:
Continuous value prediction plays a crucial role in industrial-scale recommendation systems, including tasks such as predicting users' watch-time and estimating the gross merchandise value (GMV) in e-commerce transactions. However, it remains challenging due to the highly complex and long-tailed nature of the data distributions. Existing generative approaches rely on rigid parametric distribution assumptions, which fundamentally limits their performance when such assumptions misalign with real-world data. Overly simplified forms cannot adequately model real-world complexities, while more intricate assumptions often suffer from poor scalability and generalization.
  To address these challenges, we propose a residual quantization (RQ)-based sequence learning framework that represents target continuous values as a sum of ordered quantization codes, predicted recursively from coarse to fine granularity with diminishing quantization errors. We introduce a representation learning objective that aligns RQ code embedding space with the ordinal structure of target values, allowing the model to capture continuous representations for quantization codes and further improving prediction accuracy. We perform extensive evaluations on public benchmarks for lifetime value (LTV) and watch-time prediction, alongside a large-scale online experiment for GMV prediction on an industrial short-video recommendation platform. The results consistently show that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods, while demonstrating strong generalization across diverse continuous value prediction tasks in recommendation systems.
papers.headline: 極端な数値のバラツキも「段階的な絞り込み」で正確に予測
papers.one_liner: 動画の視聴時間や売上のような、バラツキが大きく予測困難な数値（連続値）を、まず「大まかな値」から予測し、徐々に「細かい値」へと段階的に絞り込んでいく（残差量子化）ことで精度を飛躍的に高める技術です。
key_points: 「AIの思い込み（統計モデルの仮定）」に縛られず、実際のデータの複雑な形に合わせて柔軟に学習できる。
「まずは100km単位、次に1km単位、最後に1m単位」のように、解像度を上げながら段階的に予測するため、誤差が蓄積しにくい。
数値の「大小関係」をAIが正しく理解する仕組みを導入しており、似たような数値の予測ミスを防げる。
Eコマースの取引額や視聴時間など、従来のAIが苦手としていた「一部の極端なデータ（ロングテール）」にも強い。
計算の効率（スケーラビリティ）と、新しいデータへの対応力（汎用性）を両立しており、実務での導入ハードルが低い。
who_should_read: PM/プロダクトマネージャー
application_ideas: 工場検査の場面で、部品の「わずかな摩耗量」を予測する際、まず大まかな劣化レベルを特定してからナノメートル単位の数値を予測することで、交換時期の判断ミスを減らせそう。
インフラ点検において、橋梁のひび割れ深さや腐食の進行度を予測する際、過去の膨大なバラツキがあるデータからでも「段階的な絞り込み」によって現実的な数値を算出できそう。
BIMデータと連携し、建物の資材発注量を予測する際、天候や工程の変動による「不規則なブレ」を考慮した精度の高い見積もりが実現できそう。

papers.title: SubspaceAD: Training-Free Few-Shot Anomaly Detection via Subspace Modeling
papers.abstract: Detecting visual anomalies in industrial inspection often requires training with only a few normal images per category. Recent few-shot methods achieve strong results employing foundation-model features, but typically rely on memory banks, auxiliary datasets, or multi-modal tuning of vision-language models. We therefore question whether such complexity is necessary given the feature representations of vision foundation models. To answer this question, we introduce SubspaceAD, a training-free method, that operates in two simple stages. First, patch-level features are extracted from a small set of normal images by a frozen DINOv2 backbone. Second, a Principal Component Analysis (PCA) model is fit to these features to estimate the low-dimensional subspace of normal variations. At inference, anomalies are detected via the reconstruction residual with respect to this subspace, producing interpretable and statistically grounded anomaly scores. Despite its simplicity, SubspaceAD achieves state-of-the-art performance across one-shot and few-shot settings without training, prompt tuning, or memory banks. In the one-shot anomaly detection setting, SubspaceAD achieves image-level and pixel-level AUROC of 98.0% and 97.6% on the MVTec-AD dataset, and 93.3% and 98.3% on the VisA dataset, respectively, surpassing prior state-of-the-art results. Code and demo are available at https://github.com/CLendering/SubspaceAD.
papers.headline: わずか1枚の正常写真で、製品の異常を即座に見つけられる
papers.one_liner: 正常な写真が1〜数枚あれば、AIの追加学習（ファインチューニング）なしで製品の傷や汚れを検出できます。最新の画像認識AIが捉えた特徴から「正常な状態の範囲」を数学的に計算し、そこから外れた部分を異常と見なすシンプルな仕組みです。
key_points: AIに学習させる手間が一切不要なため、新しい製品ラインにも即日導入できる
正常な画像が1枚あるだけで検品を開始でき、多品種少量生産の現場に極めて強い
どこが異常なのかを画像上で可視化できるため、人間がチェックする際の納得感が高い
膨大なデータを溜め込むデータベースが不要で、システムの動作が軽く低コストで運用できる
世界最高水準の精度を記録しており、小さな傷や部品の欠落の見落としを大幅に減らせる
who_should_read: PM/プロダクトマネージャー
application_ideas: 工場の生産ラインで、新製品の良品サンプルを1枚撮影するだけで、その直後から傷や異物混入を自動検知する「即時検品カメラ」として活用。
インフラ点検において、健全な状態の壁面や鉄骨の写真を数枚登録し、ドローン映像からひび割れや腐食を自動でマーキングする診断支援ツールに活用。
物流倉庫の入庫時に、正しい梱包状態の写真を1枚用意し、荷崩れや外装のダメージを瞬時に判別する自動ゲートに活用。

papers.title: LineGraph2Road: Structural Graph Reasoning on Line Graphs for Road Network Extraction
papers.abstract: The accurate and automatic extraction of roads from satellite imagery is critical for applications in navigation and urban planning, significantly reducing the need for manual annotation. Many existing methods decompose this task into keypoint extraction and connectedness prediction, but often struggle to capture long-range dependencies and complex topologies. Here, we propose LineGraph2Road, a framework that improves connectedness prediction by formulating it as binary classification over edges in a constructed global but sparse Euclidean graph, where nodes are keypoints extracted from segmentation masks and edges connect node pairs within a predefined distance threshold, representing potential road segments. To better learn structural link representation, we transform the original graph into its corresponding line graph and apply a Graph Transformer on it for connectedness prediction. This formulation overcomes the limitations of endpoint-embedding fusion on set-isomorphic links, enabling rich link representations and effective relational reasoning over the global structure. Additionally, we introduce an overpass/underpass head to resolve multi-level crossings and a coupled NMS strategy to preserve critical connections. We evaluate LineGraph2Road on three benchmarks: City-scale, SpaceNet, and Global-scale, and show that it achieves state-of-the-art results on two key metrics, TOPO-F1 and APLS. It also captures fine visual details critical for real-world deployment. We will make our code publicly available.
papers.headline: 衛星写真から「つながりの正しい」道路地図を自動生成
papers.one_liner: 衛星写真から道路ネットワークを自動抽出する技術で、道路の交点を「点」、道を「線」としたグラフ（網目構造）として解析することで、複雑な道路のつながりや立体交差も正確に再現できます。
key_points: 画像が一部不鮮明でも、AIが道路の「つながり」を推論して途切れのない地図を作れる
複雑な立体交差（上下の重なり）を正しく判別できる専用の解析機能を搭載している
広範囲のデータから道路の法則性を学習するため、都市全体の地図作成を一貫して行える
人手による地図のトレース（なぞり書き）作業を大幅に自動化し、コストを削減できる
カーナビや都市計画にそのまま活用可能な、構造的に正しいネットワークデータが得られる
who_should_read: PM/プロダクトマネージャー
application_ideas: 工場の配管図面やプラントの3D点群データにおいて、複雑に絡み合うパイプの「つながり」を自動特定し、系統図を自動作成する。
橋梁やトンネルの点検において、個別のひび割れを線として捉え、それらがどう連結して構造的なリスク（大きな亀裂）を形成しているかを自動診断する。
建設現場の配筋検査において、撮影画像から鉄筋が正しく結束され、設計通りのネットワークを形成しているかを自動照査する。

papers.title: AgenticOCR: Parsing Only What You Need for Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.abstract: The expansion of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) into multimodal domains has intensified the challenge for processing complex visual documents, such as financial reports. While page-level chunking and retrieval is a natural starting point, it creates a critical bottleneck: delivering entire pages to the generator introduces excessive extraneous context. This not only overloads the generator's attention mechanism but also dilutes the most salient evidence. Moreover, compressing these information-rich pages into a limited visual token budget further increases the risk of hallucinations. To address this, we introduce AgenticOCR, a dynamic parsing paradigm that transforms optical character recognition (OCR) from a static, full-text process into a query-driven, on-demand extraction system. By autonomously analyzing document layout in a "thinking with images" manner, AgenticOCR identifies and selectively recognizes regions of interest. This approach performs on-demand decompression of visual tokens precisely where needed, effectively decoupling retrieval granularity from rigid page-level chunking. AgenticOCR has the potential to serve as the "third building block" of the visual document RAG stack, operating alongside and enhancing standard Embedding and Reranking modules. Experimental results demonstrate that AgenticOCR improves both the efficiency and accuracy of visual RAG systems, achieving expert-level performance in long document understanding. Code and models are available at https://github.com/OpenDataLab/AgenticOCR.
papers.headline: 膨大な資料から「必要な情報だけ」を抜き出しAIの嘘を激減させる
papers.one_liner: AIが資料のレイアウトを人間のように理解し、質問に関係する箇所だけをピンポイントで高精細に読み取ることで、AIの思い込み（ハルシネーション）を防ぎ、回答の正確性を高める技術です。
key_points: ページ全体を読み込まず必要な図表だけを抽出するため、AIが一度に処理できる情報量の制限を回避できる
資料のどこに何が書かれているかをAIが自ら判断し、重要な箇所だけを拡大して読み取る「動的な読み取り」が可能
質問に関係のない余計な情報を無視できるため、AIが混乱せず回答の根拠が明確になる
複雑なレイアウトや細かい数値が並ぶ表でも、必要な部分に絞って解析することで読み取りミスが減る
既存の文書検索システム（RAG）に「第三の部品」として組み込むだけで、回答精度を専門家レベルに向上できる
who_should_read: 図面認識・照査AIエンジニア
PM/プロダクトマネージャー
application_ideas: 数百ページの設計仕様書の中から、特定の工種に関する数値基準だけを自動で抜き出し、施工計画書との不整合を瞬時にチェックする。
過去10年分の橋梁点検報告書から、特定の劣化箇所（ひび割れ等）の記述と写真だけを抽出・集約し、補修の優先順位付けを支援する。
工場の複雑な設備マニュアルから、発生したエラーコードに関連する配線図や部品リストだけをスマホ画面に即座に表示させる現場支援ツール。

papers.title: Action-Geometry Prediction with 3D Geometric Prior for Bimanual Manipulation
papers.abstract: Bimanual manipulation requires policies that can reason about 3D geometry, anticipate how it evolves under action, and generate smooth, coordinated motions. However, existing methods typically rely on 2D features with limited spatial awareness, or require explicit point clouds that are difficult to obtain reliably in real-world settings. At the same time, recent 3D geometric foundation models show that accurate and diverse 3D structure can be reconstructed directly from RGB images in a fast and robust manner. We leverage this opportunity and propose a framework that builds bimanual manipulation directly on a pre-trained 3D geometric foundation model. Our policy fuses geometry-aware latents, 2D semantic features, and proprioception into a unified state representation, and uses diffusion model to jointly predict a future action chunk and a future 3D latent that decodes into a dense pointmap. By explicitly predicting how the 3D scene will evolve together with the action sequence, the policy gains strong spatial understanding and predictive capability using only RGB observations. We evaluate our method both in simulation on the RoboTwin benchmark and in real-world robot executions. Our approach consistently outperforms 2D-based and point-cloud-based baselines, achieving state-of-the-art performance in manipulation success, inter-arm coordination, and 3D spatial prediction accuracy. Code is available at https://github.com/Chongyang-99/GAP.git.
papers.headline: 普通のカメラでロボットが3D空間を把握し両手作業を器用にこなす
papers.one_liner: 高価な3Dスキャナを使わず、普通のカメラ映像から「物体がどう動くか」を3D予測（ジオメトリ予測）することで、ロボットの両手をスムーズに連動させる技術です。
key_points: 特殊な3Dセンサー（LiDAR等）が不要になり、安価なカメラだけで高度な3D操作が可能になる
AIが「次に物体がどういう形になるか」を予測するため、複雑な作業でも見落としやミスが減る
ロボットの右腕と左腕がぶつからないよう、空間を把握しながらスムーズに協力作業ができる
あらかじめ大量の3Dデータを学習したAI（基礎モデル）を使うため、未知の道具や環境にも強い
現実のロボット実験において、従来の手法よりも圧倒的に高い作業成功率を記録している
who_should_read: PM/プロダクトマネージャー
application_ideas: 工場の組み立てラインにおいて、従来の2Dカメラでは難しかった「ケーブルの配線」や「柔軟なパーツの取り付け」を自動化する
インフラ点検や災害復旧の現場で、2本の腕を持つロボットが周囲の瓦礫の形を3Dで予測しながら、安全に除去・移動させる
BIMデータと連携し、建設現場のドローンや搬送ロボットが「今の現場の形」をカメラだけで即座に認識し、障害物を避けながら作業する

papers.title: RUMAD: Reinforcement-Unifying Multi-Agent Debate
papers.abstract:
Multi-agent debate (MAD) systems leverage collective intelligence to enhance reasoning capabilities, yet existing approaches struggle to simultaneously optimize accuracy, consensus formation, and computational efficiency. Static topology methods lack adaptability to task complexity variations, while external LLM-based coordination risks introducing privileged knowledge that compromises debate neutrality. This work presents RUMAD (Reinforcement-Unifying Multi-Agent Debate), a novel framework that formulates dynamic communication topology control in MAD as a reinforcement learning (RL) problem.
  RUMAD employs a content-agnostic observation scheme that captures high-level debate dynamics avoiding access to raw agent reasoning content. RUMAD uses a multi-objective reward to model solution quality, cohesion and efficiency. A PPO-trained controller dynamically adjusts edge weights in the communication graph, while a dual-threshold mechanism enables fine-grained control over both agent activation and information visibility.
  Experimental evaluation across MMLU, GSM8K, and GPQA benchmarks demonstrates that RUMAD achieves substantial efficiency gains, reducing token costs by over 80\%, while still improving reasoning accuracy compared to single LLM model and multiple MAD baselines. Notably, RUMAD trained exclusively on MMLU exhibits robust zero-shot generalization to out-of-domain (OOD) tasks, indicating that the learned communication strategies capture task-independent principles of effective multi-agent coordination. These results establish RUMAD as a efficient and robust approach for deploying multi-agent reasoning application with practical resource constraints.
papers.headline: AI同士の議論を最適化し、コスト8割減で正解を導き出す
papers.one_liner: 複数のAIに議論させて結論を出す仕組みにおいて、強化学習（AIが試行錯誤で上達する手法）を用いて「誰が発言し、誰がそれを見るか」を自動制御することで、通信コスト（トークン代）を80％以上削減しながら精度を高める技術です。
key_points: AI同士の無駄なやり取りを省き、運用コストを従来の5分の1以下に抑えられる
議論の「中身」ではなく「対話のパターン」を見て制御するため、情報の機密性を保ちやすい
一度学んだ「効率的な議論の進め方」は、未経験の新しい分野の課題解決にもそのまま活用できる
問題の難易度に応じて、議論に参加するAIの人数や情報の見せ方をリアルタイムで調整できる
単独のAIでは判断が難しい複雑な推論問題でも、複数AIの協力により正答率を底上げできる
who_should_read: PM/プロダクトマネージャー
application_ideas: 図面チェックの場面で、意匠・構造・設備の専門AIを議論させ、矛盾箇所の指摘を最小限の通信コストで高速に実行する。
工場検査の判定で、合格・不合格の判断が分かれるグレーゾーン画像のみを複数のAIで合議制にし、通常品は1台のAIで処理することで、精度維持と低コストを両立させる。
橋梁などのインフラ点検において、過去の損傷データと現在の画像を複数のAIに分析させ、最も信頼性の高い補修優先順位を効率的なディスカッションを通じて策定する。

papers.title: Time Series Foundation Models as Strong Baselines in Transportation Forecasting: A Large-Scale Benchmark Analysis
papers.abstract: Accurate forecasting of transportation dynamics is essential for urban mobility and infrastructure planning. Although recent work has achieved strong performance with deep learning models, these methods typically require dataset-specific training, architecture design and hyper-parameter tuning. This paper evaluates whether general-purpose time-series foundation models can serve as forecasters for transportation tasks by benchmarking the zero-shot performance of the state-of-the-art model, Chronos-2, across ten real-world datasets covering highway traffic volume and flow, urban traffic speed, bike-sharing demand, and electric vehicle charging station data. Under a consistent evaluation protocol, we find that, even without any task-specific fine-tuning, Chronos-2 delivers state-of-the-art or competitive accuracy across most datasets, frequently outperforming classical statistical baselines and specialized deep learning architectures, particularly at longer horizons. Beyond point forecasting, we evaluate its native probabilistic outputs using prediction-interval coverage and sharpness, demonstrating that Chronos-2 also provides useful uncertainty quantification without dataset-specific training. In general, this study supports the adoption of time-series foundation models as a key baseline for transportation forecasting research.
papers.headline: 学習なしで交通渋滞や需要をAIが即座に高精度予測
papers.one_liner: 特定の場所のデータで追加学習（ファインチューニング）をさせなくても、世界中のデータを学んだ「時系列AI」が交通量やEV充電需要をプロ並みに予測できる仕組みです。
key_points: 現場ごとのAIモデル開発や、複雑な設定の調整（ハイパーパラメータチューニング）が不要になる
数時間から数日先までの長期的な予測において、従来の専用AIよりも高い精度を出すことができる
「何％の確率で渋滞するか」といった予測の自信（不確実性）も同時に出力できるため、リスク判断に使いやすい
道路の交通量だけでなく、シェアサイクルやEV充電スタンドの需要予測など、異なるデータにもそのまま転用できる
既存の解析ツールを導入する前の「基準（ベースライン）」として、低コストで即座に導入・比較が可能
who_should_read: PM/プロダクトマネージャー
application_ideas: 工場の搬入車両の予測に導入し、事前の学習コストをかけずにトラックの待機時間を削減する人員配置計画を自動作成する。
インフラ点検の現場で、交通量の将来変化を予測し、通行規制の影響が最も少ない最適な工事時期をシミュレーションする。
BIM/CIMデータと連携し、建設予定の商業施設周辺で発生する将来の交通渋滞リスクを、設計段階で予測して対策を検討する。

papers.title: OPTIAGENT: A Physics-Driven Agentic Framework for Automated Optical Design
papers.abstract: Optical design is the process of configuring optical elements to precisely manipulate light for high-fidelity imaging. It is inherently a highly non-convex optimization problem that relies heavily on human heuristic expertise and domain-specific knowledge. While Large Language Models (LLMs) possess extensive optical knowledge, their capabilities in leveraging the knowledge in designing lens system remain significantly constrained. This work represents the first attempt to employ LLMs in the field of optical design. We bridge the expertise gap by enabling users without formal optical training to successfully develop functional lens systems. Concretely, we curate a comprehensive dataset, named OptiDesignQA, which encompasses both classical lens systems sourced from standard optical textbooks and novel configurations generated by automated design algorithms for training and evaluation. Furthermore, we inject domain-specific optical expertise into the LLM through a hybrid objective of full-system synthesis and lens completion. To align the model with optical principles, we employ Group Relative Policy Optimization Done Right (DrGRPO) guided by Optical Lexicographic Reward for physics-driven policy alignment. This reward system incorporates structural format rewards, physical feasibility rewards, light-manipulation accuracy, and LLM-based heuristics. Finally, our model integrates with specialized optical optimization routines for end-to-end fine-tuning and precision refinement. We benchmark our proposed method against both traditional optimization-based automated design algorithms and LLM counterparts, and experimental results show the superiority of our method.
papers.headline: 専門知識なしで、高性能なレンズ設計が自動で行える
papers.one_liner: 長年の経験が必要なレンズ（光学系）の設計を、物理法則を理解したAI（物理駆動エージェント）が自動で行い、専門知識がない人でも実用的な設計図を生成できる技術です。
key_points: 熟練者の「勘」をAIが学習し、誰でもプロ級のレンズ設計案を作成できる
物理的な正しさをAIが自動判定するため、実現不可能な「AIの思い込み」を防げる
設計の初期構想から細かな数値の追い込みまで、一気通貫で自動化が可能
膨大な教科書データと最新の最適化手法を組み合わせ、最適なレンズ構成を提案する
既存の専門解析ソフトとAIが連携し、そのまま製造に回せるレベルの精度を実現する
tags: 光学シミュレーション

papers.title: Data Driven Optimization of GPU efficiency for Distributed LLM Adapter Serving
papers.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) adapters enable low-cost model specialization, but introduce complex caching and scheduling challenges in distributed serving systems where hundreds of adapters must be hosted concurrently. While prior work has largely focused on latency minimization, resource efficiency through throughput maximization remains underexplored. This paper presents a data-driven pipeline that, for a given workload, computes an adapter placement that serves the workload with the minimum number of GPUs while avoiding request starvation and GPU memory errors. To that end, the approach identifies the maximum feasible throughput attainable on each GPU by leveraging accurate performance predictions learned from real serving behavior. The proposed pipeline integrates three components: (i) a Digital Twin (DT) tailored to LLM-adapter serving, (ii) a distilled machine learning (ML) model trained on DT-generated data, and (iii) a greedy placement algorithm that exploits ML-based performance estimates to maximize GPU efficiency. The DT emulates real system dynamics with high fidelity, achieving below 5% throughput estimation error while executing up to 90 times faster than full LLM benchmarking across both predictable and unpredictable workloads. The learned ML models further accelerate performance estimation with marginal accuracy degradation, enabling scalable optimization. Experimental results demonstrate that the pipeline substantially improves GPU efficiency by reducing the number of GPUs required to sustain target workloads. Beyond GPU efficiency, the pipeline can be adapted to alternative objectives, such as latency minimization, highlighting its versatility for future large-scale LLM serving infrastructures.
papers.headline: 少ないGPUで数百の特化型AIを効率よく動かせるようになる
papers.one_liner: 特定の業務に特化した複数のAI（アダプター）を動かす際、AIの「分身（デジタルツイン）」を使って最適な配置をシミュレーションすることで、最小限の計算機（GPU）で安定した運用を可能にする技術です。
key_points: 高価な計算機（GPU）の台数を最小限に抑えられるため、AIの運用コストを大幅に削減できる
「システムのデジタルツイン」を使うことで、実際の環境で試すより90倍速く、最適な設定を見つけ出せる
AIが急に重くなる、メモリが足りなくなるといった「予期せぬトラブル」を5%以下の誤差で事前に予測できる
数百種類の「専門特化AI」を一つのシステムに相乗りさせても、処理が渋滞せずにスムーズに動かせる
処理の速さ（応答時間）だけでなく、効率（さばける量）を重視した賢いスケジューリングが可能になる
who_should_read: PM/プロダクトマネージャー

工場の品質検査において、製品ラインや型番ごとに異なる「外観検査用AIアダプター」を一つのサーバーに集約し、設備投資を抑えつつ検査の待ち時間をゼロにする。
膨大な過去の図面や仕様書から特定の部材を探す際、案件や顧客ごとにカスタマイズされた「専門用語理解AI」を効率よく切り替えて、検索サーバーの負荷を最適化する。

papers.title: Thinking with Images as Continuous Actions: Numerical Visual Chain-of-Thought
papers.abstract: Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) increasingly rely on visual chain-of-thought to perform region-grounded reasoning over images. However, existing approaches ground regions via either textified coordinates-causing modality mismatch and semantic fragmentation or fixed-granularity patches that both limit precise region selection and often require non-trivial architectural changes. In this paper, we propose Numerical Visual Chain-of-Thought (NV-CoT), a framework that enables MLLMs to reason over images using continuous numerical coordinates. NV-CoT expands the MLLM action space from discrete vocabulary tokens to a continuous Euclidean space, allowing models to directly generate bounding-box coordinates as actions with only minimal architectural modification. The framework supports both supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. In particular, we replace categorical token policies with a Gaussian (or Laplace) policy over coordinates and introduce stochasticity via reparameterized sampling, making NV-CoT fully compatible with GRPO-style policy optimization. Extensive experiments on three benchmarks against eight representative visual reasoning baselines demonstrate that NV-CoT significantly improves localization precision and final answer accuracy, while also accelerating training convergence, validating the effectiveness of continuous-action visual reasoning in MLLMs. The code is available in https://github.com/kesenzhao/NV-CoT.
papers.headline: AIが写真の「ここ！」をミリ単位で正確に特定し判断できる
papers.one_liner: 画像と文字の両方を理解できるAI（マルチモーダルLLM）が、画像内の位置を文字（座標のテキスト）ではなく直接的な数値（連続値）として扱うことで、対象物の特定精度と判断能力を大幅に高める技術です。
key_points: 画像の中の小さな部品や細かな傷を、従来のAIよりもはるかに高い精度でピンポイントに特定できます。
「座標を文字に直す」という余計なステップを省いたため、AIの学習スピードが向上し、効率的に賢くなります。
AIが答えを出すまでの「思考プロセス」の中で、関連する場所を正確に指し示しながら論理的に判断できます。
既存のAIモデルの基本構造を大きく変えることなく導入できるため、実務への応用がスムーズです。
AIが試行錯誤して成長する強化学習との相性が良く、特定の業務に合わせた高度な最適化が可能です。

PM/プロダクトマネージャー
application_ideas: 図面チェックの場面で、壁と柱の重なりやミリ単位の寸法ズレをAIが自動で見つけ出し、修正箇所を正確にマークする機能として活用すれば、見落としが激減します。
インフラ点検の際、ドローンが撮影した橋梁の画像から「ひび割れ」の正確な範囲をAIが囲い、その面積や深刻度を即座に計算するツールとして使えば、点検報告書の作成時間が大幅に短縮できます。

papers.title: BuildAnyPoint: 3D Building Structured Abstraction from Diverse Point Clouds
papers.abstract: We introduce BuildAnyPoint, a novel generative framework for structured 3D building reconstruction from point clouds with diverse distributions, such as those captured by airborne LiDAR and Structure-from-Motion. To recover artist-created building abstraction in this highly underconstrained setting, we capitalize on the role of explicit 3D generative priors in autoregressive mesh generation. Specifically, we design a Loosely Cascaded Diffusion Transformer (Loca-DiT) that initially recovers the underlying distribution from noisy or sparse points, followed by autoregressively encapsulating them into compact meshes. We first formulate distribution recovery as a conditional generation task by training latent diffusion models conditioned on input point clouds, and then tailor a decoder-only transformer for conditional autoregressive mesh generation based on the recovered point clouds. Our method delivers substantial qualitative and quantitative improvements over prior building abstraction methods. Furthermore, the effectiveness of our approach is evidenced by the strong performance of its recovered point clouds on building point cloud completion benchmarks, which exhibit improved surface accuracy and distribution uniformity.
papers.headline: スカスカな3D点群から、きれいな建物の箱モデルが作れる
papers.one_liner: ノイズや欠損が多い3D点群（レーザースキャンの点データ）から、カチッとした建物の3Dモデル（メッシュデータ）を自動生成する技術です。AIが「建物らしい形」を推論して補完（拡散モデルによる点群復元）した上で、効率的な形へ整える（自動回帰型メッシュ生成）2段階の処理で、高品質な抽象化を実現します。
key_points: ドローンや航空機からの「ガタガタで抜け漏れがある点群」を、きれいな直線と面を持つモデルに変換できる
従来は手作業で数日かかっていた「点群からBIMモデルへの書き起こし」作業をAIで自動化できる
AIが建物の構造を理解しているため、スキャンできなかった死角の壁面や屋根も「それらしく」補完してくれる
データが軽量なポリゴン形式に変換されるため、Web閲覧や大規模な都市シミュレーションで扱いやすくなる
最新の画像生成AIの仕組み（拡散モデル）を応用し、従来の技術では難しかった複雑な形状の建物にも対応できる

リノベーション現場の現況測量において、簡易LiDARで撮影したノイズの多いデータから「きれいな壁面と屋根の箱モデル」を自動作成し、設計のたたき台として活用する
インフラ点検の場面で、欠損のある点群データから本来あるべき構造物の形状を推定・再現し、変形やひずみを定量評価するための比較基準モデルとして利用する

papers.title: Jailbreak Foundry: From Papers to Runnable Attacks for Reproducible Benchmarking
papers.abstract: Jailbreak techniques for large language models (LLMs) evolve faster than benchmarks, making robustness estimates stale and difficult to compare across papers due to drift in datasets, harnesses, and judging protocols. We introduce JAILBREAK FOUNDRY (JBF), a system that addresses this gap via a multi-agent workflow to translate jailbreak papers into executable modules for immediate evaluation within a unified harness. JBF features three core components: (i) JBF-LIB for shared contracts and reusable utilities; (ii) JBF-FORGE for the multi-agent paper-to-module translation; and (iii) JBF-EVAL for standardizing evaluations. Across 30 reproduced attacks, JBF achieves high fidelity with a mean (reproduced-reported) attack success rate (ASR) deviation of +0.26 percentage points. By leveraging shared infrastructure, JBF reduces attack-specific implementation code by nearly half relative to original repositories and achieves an 82.5% mean reused-code ratio. This system enables a standardized AdvBench evaluation of all 30 attacks across 10 victim models using a consistent GPT-4o judge. By automating both attack integration and standardized evaluation, JBF offers a scalable solution for creating living benchmarks that keep pace with the rapidly shifting security landscape.
papers.headline: AIへの攻撃手法を自動で再現し、最新の安全性をすぐ評価できる
papers.one_liner: 最新のAIを「だます」攻撃手法（ジェイルブレイク）を記述した論文を、AIエージェントが自動でプログラムへ変換し、自社のAIがその攻撃に耐えられるかを統一された基準で即座にテストできる仕組みです。
key_points: 最新のAI攻撃手法をいち早くプログラムとして再現し、自社システムでの検証が可能になります。
バラバラだった評価基準を統一し、自社のAIがどれくらい「だまされにくいか」を正確に数値化できます。
セキュリティテスト用のプログラム作成工数を約半分に削減し、効率的な検証体制を構築できます。
AI同士が協力して論文からコードを生成するため、専門知識がなくても最新の脆弱性対策に追随できます。
攻撃手法が進化し続ける「いたちごっこ」の状態でも、常に最新のベンチマーク（評価指標）を維持できます。
who_should_read: PM/プロダクトマネージャー
application_ideas: 現場の施工管理AIチャットボットにおいて、部外者による機密情報の聞き出しや安全規定を無視するような指示（悪意のある入力）への耐性を、最新の攻撃パターンで自動診断する。
工場の熟練技能を学習させたナレッジ共有AIを導入する際、競合他社にノウハウを不正に抽出されるリスクがないか、稼働前に一括して脆弱性チェックを行う。
インフラ点検の報告書作成AIが、悪意あるユーザーの誘導によって「異常なし」と嘘の判定を下してしまうような特殊な入力パターン（プロンプト注入）を、事前検証で網羅的に洗い出す。

papers.title: Bandwidth-adaptive Cloud-Assisted 360-Degree 3D Perception for Autonomous Vehicles
papers.abstract: A key challenge for autonomous driving lies in maintaining real-time situational awareness regarding surrounding obstacles under strict latency constraints. The high processing requirements coupled with limited onboard computational resources can cause delay issues, particularly in complex urban settings. To address this, we propose leveraging Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication to partially offload processing to the cloud, where compute resources are abundant, thus reducing overall latency. Our approach utilizes transformer-based models to fuse multi-camera sensor data into a comprehensive Bird's-Eye View (BEV) representation, enabling accurate 360-degree 3D object detection. The computation is dynamically split between the vehicle and the cloud based on the number of layers processed locally and the quantization level of the features. To further reduce network load, we apply feature vector clipping and compression prior to transmission. In a real-world experimental evaluation, our hybrid strategy achieved a 72 \% reduction in end-to-end latency compared to a traditional onboard solution. To adapt to fluctuating network conditions, we introduce a dynamic optimization algorithm that selects the split point and quantization level to maximize detection accuracy while satisfying real-time latency constraints. Trace-based evaluation under realistic bandwidth variability shows that this adaptive approach improves accuracy by up to 20 \% over static parameterization with the same latency performance.
papers.headline: 自動運転の反応を7割速くし、360度の障害物を正確に見つける
papers.one_liner: 車載コンピュータの負担を、通信状況に応じてクラウドへ賢く分散（計算の肩代わり）させることで、周囲360度の状況を素早く正確に把握する技術です。
key_points: 車側の処理能力が低くても、クラウドの力を借りて高度な3D検知ができる
通信の混み具合に合わせて、送るデータの量や質をAIが自動で調整してくれる

papers.title: From Flat Logs to Causal Graphs: Hierarchical Failure Attribution for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: LLM-powered Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in complex domains but suffer from inherent fragility and opaque failure mechanisms. Existing failure attribution methods, whether relying on direct prompting, costly replays, or supervised fine-tuning, typically treat execution logs as flat sequences. This linear perspective fails to disentangle the intricate causal links inherent to MAS, leading to weak observability and ambiguous responsibility boundaries. To address these challenges, we propose CHIEF, a novel framework that transforms chaotic trajectories into a structured hierarchical causal graph. It then employs hierarchical oracle-guided backtracking to efficiently prune the search space via sybthesized virtual oracles. Finally, it implements counterfactual attribution via a progressive causal screening strategy to rigorously distinguish true root causes from propagated symptoms. Experiments on Who&When benchmark show that CHIEF outperforms eight strong and state-of-the-art baselines on both agent- and step-level accuracy. Ablation studies further confirm the critical role of each proposed module.

papers.title: Enhancing Vision-Language Navigation with Multimodal Event Knowledge from Real-World Indoor Tour Videos
papers.abstract: Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) agents often struggle with long-horizon reasoning in unseen environments, particularly when facing ambiguous, coarse-grained instructions. While recent advances use knowledge graph to enhance reasoning, the potential of multimodal event knowledge inspired by human episodic memory remains underexplored. In this work, we propose an event-centric knowledge enhancement strategy for automated process knowledge mining and feature fusion to solve coarse-grained instruction and long-horizon reasoning in VLN task. First, we construct YE-KG, the first large-scale multimodal spatiotemporal knowledge graph, with over 86k nodes and 83k edges, derived from real-world indoor videos. By leveraging multimodal large language models (i.e., LLaVa, GPT4), we extract unstructured video streams into structured semantic-action-effect events to serve as explicit episodic memory. Second, we introduce STE-VLN, which integrates the above graph into VLN models via a Coarse-to-Fine Hierarchical Retrieval mechanism. This allows agents to retrieve causal event sequences and dynamically fuse them with egocentric visual observations. Experiments on REVERIE, R2R, and R2R-CE benchmarks demonstrate the efficiency of our event-centric strategy, outperforming state-of-the-art approaches across diverse action spaces. Our data and code are available on the project website https://sites.google.com/view/y-event-kg/.

papers.title: See, Act, Adapt: Active Perception for Unsupervised Cross-Domain Visual Adaptation via Personalized VLM-Guided Agent
papers.abstract: Pre-trained perception models excel in generic image domains but degrade significantly in novel environments like indoor scenes. The conventional remedy is fine-tuning on downstream data which incurs catastrophic forgetting of prior knowledge and demands costly, scene-specific annotations. We propose a paradigm shift through Sea$^2$ (See, Act, Adapt): rather than adapting the perception modules themselves, we adapt how they are deployed through an intelligent pose-control agent. Sea$^2$ keeps all perception modules frozen, requiring no downstream labels during training, and uses only scalar perceptual feedback to navigate the agent toward informative viewpoints. Specially, we transform a vision-language model (VLM) into a low-level pose controller through a two-stage training pipeline: first fine-tuning it on rule-based exploration trajectories that systematically probe indoor scenes, and then refining the policy via unsupervised reinforcement learning that constructs rewards from the perception module's outputs and confidence. Unlike prior active perception methods that couple exploration with specific models or collect data for retraining them, Sea$^2$ directly leverages off-the-shelf perception models for various tasks without the need for retraining. We conducted experiments on three visual perception tasks, including visual grounding, segmentation and 3D box estimation, with performance improvements of 13.54%, 15.92% and 27.68% respectively on dataset ReplicaCAD.

papers.title: Look Carefully: Adaptive Visual Reinforcements in Multimodal Large Language Models for Hallucination Mitigation
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in vision-language reasoning, yet they remain vulnerable to hallucination, where generated content deviates from visual evidence. Existing mitigation strategies either require costly supervision during training or introduce additional latency at inference time. Recent vision enhancement methods attempt to address this issue by reinforcing visual tokens during decoding, but they typically inject all tokens indiscriminately, which causes interference from background regions and distracts the model from critical cues. To overcome this challenge, we propose Adaptive Visual Reinforcement (AIR), a training-free framework for MLLMs. AIR consists of two components. Prototype-based token reduction condenses the large pool of visual tokens into a compact subset to suppress redundancy. OT-guided patch reinforcement quantifies the alignment between hidden states and patch embeddings to selectively integrate the most consistent patches into feed-forward layers. As a result, AIR enhances the model's reliance on salient visual information and effectively mitigates hallucination. Extensive experiments across representative MLLMs demonstrate that AIR substantially reduces hallucination while preserving general capabilities, establishing it as an effective solution for building reliable MLLMs.

papers.title: Experience-Guided Self-Adaptive Cascaded Agents for Breast Cancer Screening and Diagnosis with Reduced Biopsy Referrals
papers.abstract: We propose an experience-guided cascaded multi-agent framework for Breast Ultrasound Screening and Diagnosis, called BUSD-Agent, that aims to reduce diagnostic escalation and unnecessary biopsy referrals. Our framework models screening and diagnosis as a two-stage, selective decision-making process. A lightweight `screening clinic' agent, restricted to classification models as tools, selectively filters out benign and normal cases from further diagnostic escalation when malignancy risk and uncertainty are estimated as low. Cases that have higher risks are escalated to the `diagnostic clinic' agent, which integrates richer perception and radiological description tools to make a secondary decision on biopsy referral. To improve agent performance, past records of pathology-confirmed outcomes along with image embeddings, model predictions, and historical agent actions are stored in a memory bank as structured decision trajectories. For each new case, BUSD-Agent retrieves similar past cases based on image, model response and confidence similarity to condition the agent's current decision policy. This enables retrieval-conditioned in-context adaptation that dynamically adjusts model trust and escalation thresholds from prior experiences without parameter updates. Evaluation across 10 breast ultrasound datasets shows that the proposed experience-guided workflow reduces diagnostic escalation in BUSD-Agent from 84.95% to 58.72% and overall biopsy referrals from 59.50% to 37.08%, compared to the same architecture without trajectory conditioning, while improving average screening specificity by 68.48% and diagnostic specificity by 6.33%.

papers.title: PseudoAct: Leveraging Pseudocode Synthesis for Flexible Planning and Action Control in Large Language Model Agents
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents typically rely on reactive decision-making paradigms such as ReAct, selecting actions conditioned on growing execution histories. While effective for short tasks, these approaches often lead to redundant tool usage, unstable reasoning, and high token consumption in complex long-horizon tasks involving branching, iteration, or multi-tool coordination. To address these limitations, this paper introduces PseudoAct, a novel framework for flexible planning and action control in LLM agents through pseudocode synthesis. Leveraging the ability of LLMs to express task-solving strategies as code, PseudoAct synthesizes a structured pseudocode plan that decomposes a task into subtasks and explicitly encodes control flow, including sequencing, conditionals, loops, parallel composition, and combinations of these logic primitives. Actions are then executed by following this global plan, making the decision logic explicit and temporally coherent. This design reduces redundant actions, prevents infinite loops, and avoids uninformative alternative exploration, enabling consistent and efficient long-horizon decision-making. Experiments on benchmark datasets show that our method significantly outperforms existing reactive agent approaches, achieving a 20.93% absolute gain in success rate on FEVER and setting a new state-of-the-art on HotpotQA.

papers.title: TRIZ-RAGNER: A Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Model for TRIZ-Aware Named Entity Recognition in Patent-Based Contradiction Mining
papers.abstract: TRIZ-based contradiction mining is a fundamental task in patent analysis and systematic innovation, as it enables the identification of improving and worsening technical parameters that drive inventive problem solving. However, existing approaches largely rely on rule-based systems or traditional machine learning models, which struggle with semantic ambiguity, domain dependency, and limited generalization when processing complex patent language. Recently, large language models (LLMs) have shown strong semantic understanding capabilities, yet their direct application to TRIZ parameter extraction remains challenging due to hallucination and insufficient grounding in structured TRIZ knowledge. To address these limitations, this paper proposes TRIZ-RAGNER, a retrieval-augmented large language model framework for TRIZ-aware named entity recognition in patent-based contradiction mining. TRIZ-RAGNER reformulates contradiction mining as a semantic-level NER task and integrates dense retrieval over a TRIZ knowledge base, cross-encoder reranking for context refinement, and structured LLM prompting to extract improving and worsening parameters from patent sentences. By injecting domain-specific TRIZ knowledge into the LLM reasoning process, the proposed framework effectively reduces semantic noise and improves extraction consistency. Experiments on the PaTRIZ dataset demonstrate that TRIZ-RAGNER consistently outperforms traditional sequence labeling models and LLM-based baselines. The proposed framework achieves a precision of 85.6%, a recall of 82.9%, and an F1-score of 84.2% in TRIZ contradiction pair identification. Compared with the strongest baseline using prompt-enhanced GPT, TRIZ-RAGNER yields an absolute F1-score improvement of 7.3 percentage points, confirming the effectiveness of retrieval-augmented TRIZ knowledge grounding for robust and accurate patent-based contradiction mining.

papers.title: FlexGuard: Continuous Risk Scoring for Strictness-Adaptive LLM Content Moderation
papers.abstract: Ensuring the safety of LLM-generated content is essential for real-world deployment. Most existing guardrail models formulate moderation as a fixed binary classification task, implicitly assuming a fixed definition of harmfulness. In practice, enforcement strictness - how conservatively harmfulness is defined and enforced - varies across platforms and evolves over time, making binary moderators brittle under shifting requirements. We first introduce FlexBench, a strictness-adaptive LLM moderation benchmark that enables controlled evaluation under multiple strictness regimes. Experiments on FlexBench reveal substantial cross-strictness inconsistency in existing moderators: models that perform well under one regime can degrade substantially under others, limiting their practical usability. To address this, we propose FlexGuard, an LLM-based moderator that outputs a calibrated continuous risk score reflecting risk severity and supports strictness-specific decisions via thresholding. We train FlexGuard via risk-alignment optimization to improve score-severity consistency and provide practical threshold selection strategies to adapt to target strictness at deployment. Experiments on FlexBench and public benchmarks demonstrate that FlexGuard achieves higher moderation accuracy and substantially improved robustness under varying strictness. We release the source code and data to support reproducibility.
